last.verdict: Opendoor's revenue rose to $1.02B, but profit per home fell and the loss widened as it loaded up on inventory financed by debt.

takeaways.label: Inventory and debt surge
takeaways.text: Inventory rose to $2.57B from $925M at year-end, with 7,596 homes held. Asset-backed debt reached about $2.4B, and operations used $1.8B of cash in nine months.

takeaways.label: Margins slipped
takeaways.text: Profit after direct selling and holding costs fell to 3.3% of revenue from 5.8% last quarter. It was $12,000 per home sold versus $22,000. The company had guided to 4%–4.5%.

takeaways.label: Bigger loss
takeaways.text: Net loss widened to $218M from $162M last quarter and $90M a year ago. Stock pay of about $108M and a $53M inventory writedown were the main drivers.

takeaways.label: Growth returns
takeaways.text: Revenue was $1.02B, up 12% from $915M a year ago and 16% from last quarter. Homes sold rose to 2,728, and 4,865 homes were bought.

history.verdict: Investors sold on a weak margin outlook despite revenue and cash-burn improvement.

reasons.label: Lower margin outlook
reasons.text: Next-quarter contribution margin guided to 4%–4.5%, below this quarter's 5.8%, blamed on seasonality.

reasons.label: Sales far below last year
reasons.text: Revenue was $883M, down about 44% from a year ago, and below analyst estimates.

reasons.label: Bigger loss, mostly stock pay
reasons.text: Net loss was $162M versus $29M a year ago, driven by about $119M of stock-based pay.
